Contributing
Easiest path: open a GitHub issue with a link to the paper (DOI / arXiv / bioRxiv / OpenReview / …) and I’ll wire it into the database. Corrections are equally welcome: wrong author lists, missing affiliations, mis-classified kind / DL / acquisition, broken hyperlinks, anything that looks off.

Advanced: edit the database directly
The site is generated from denovo.db (SQLite, the source of truth). If you’re comfortable with SQL:

Edit denovo.db with any SQLite tool (sqlite3 CLI, DB Browser for SQLite, DataGrip, …). A new paper typically needs rows in publication, publication_author, and publication_algorithm (set role to uses for a tool the paper runs rather than introduces, which keeps it out of that tool’s authors and papers); a new model also needs a row in algorithm (set kind, is_deep_learning, acquisition_mode). Affiliations cascade through country → city → affiliation and link to authors via author_affiliation.
Regenerate the human-readable SQL dump so the diff is reviewable:
sqlite3 denovo.db .dump > denovo.sql
Open a PR with both denovo.db and denovo.sql. The GitHub Action rebuilds the site and publishes to gh-pages on merge; typically live within ~3 minutes.

title: Complementary spectra
text: Several spectra of one peptide, from different fragmentation methods or charge states, interpreted jointly so that ions missing from one spectrum are supplied by another.

title: Constrained search
text: Replace the database with the set of sequences the measurement itself allows. An accurate precursor mass, a determined composition or a known peptide family bounds the candidate set tightly enough to

title: Diffusion
text: Iterative denoising: start from noise over the residue positions and refine repeatedly, so the precursor-mass constraint and the consistency of the whole sequence can be enforced at every step rather

title: Enzymatic ladder assisted
text: A protease chosen so that every peptide carries a predictable terminal residue, such as Lys-N, which turns the fragment ladder into a simpler series that is easier to read de novo.

title: Fragment ion analysis
text: Work on the fragment ions themselves before any sequence is proposed: charge state, isotope pattern and series assignment, which is what a sequencing algorithm downstream has to assume it already has.

title: Genetic algorithm
text: Candidate sequences evolved by mutation, crossover and selection against a spectrum-matching score, searching the space of peptides without building a spectrum graph.

title: GNN
text: Graph neural networks over the spectrum graph: they learn the path-scoring function that dynamic programming had to hand-code, which is what lets a path cross a fragment that was never observed.

title: Graph / DP
text: The classical formulation: peaks become nodes in a spectrum graph whose edges are residue masses, and the peptide is the best-scoring path through it, found by dynamic programming. Nearly every classi

title: Grouped spectra
text: Several spectra of the same peptide, from repeated injections, charge states or labeling channels, scored as one body of evidence instead of one spectrum at a time.

title: Heuristic
text: Hand-engineered interpretation rules rather than one global optimisation: extend a sequence peak by peak, enumerate the compositions that fit the mass, score what survives. The oldest approach here, a

title: Homology search
text: De novo sequences, errors and all, used as the query in an error-tolerant search against known proteins, so a protein that is in no database can still be identified through its relatives.

title: Hybrid de novo + database search
text: Two engines run side by side and reconciled, a de novo sequencer and a database search, each keeping the identifications the other cannot make.

title: Hybrid search
text: De novo interpretation used to drive a database search: the sequence or the tag read from the spectrum becomes the query, rather than the database enumerating candidates to score.

title: Latent imputation
text: Treats missing fragmentation as something to reconstruct rather than tolerate: latent representations of the theoretical peaks a peptide should have produced are imputed before the sequence is predict

title: Learning-to-rank
text: A ranking model over candidate peptides. The candidates come from a sequencer upstream, and the contribution is putting the right one on top, usually with a predicted spectrum to compare against.

title: Neural network
text: Neural networks outside the deep-learning lineage: the early sequence-determination networks, and small task-specific models that score one local decision, such as an ion-series assignment or a leucin

title: Peak selection
text: Deciding which peaks in a spectrum are real fragment ions before sequencing starts, by learned or evolved filters that remove noise and so shrink the search the sequencer faces.

title: Protease strategy
text: Choosing and combining proteases so that overlapping peptides cover a whole protein, and so that each peptide fragments well enough to read de novo. The method is in the digestion, not the sequencing

title: Random Forest
text: Tree ensembles, used to predict fragment-ion intensities and to combine several sequencers' output under a controlled error rate, rather than to sequence a spectrum directly.

title: Sequence assembly
text: Sequencing a whole protein rather than a peptide. Overlapping peptides are called first, then assembled into full-length sequence, which is how antibodies and protein therapeutics are sequenced withou

title: Sequence tag
text: Short, high-confidence stretches of sequence read straight off the spectrum and used as a filter or a query rather than as the final answer. A tag plus its flanking masses can identify a peptide on it

title: Spectra pair
text: Two spectra of the same peptide, from complementary fragmentation or from a paired digest, interpreted together so that one ion series fills the gaps in the other.

title: Spectral alignment / assembly
text: Reads a peptide from the relationships between spectra rather than from one spectrum alone, aligning or assembling overlapping acquisitions so that evidence missing from any single fragmentation is su

title: Spectral assembly
text: Assemble the overlapping spectra into contigs BEFORE any sequence is called, so a protein is read from the assembled evidence rather than from peptides interpreted one at a time. Sequence assembly is

title: Spectral profile
text: Each spectrum summarised as a probability profile over residues or fragment positions, from which the sequence is read as the most likely path rather than by matching peaks one at a time.

title: Template-guided assembly
text: De novo peptide reads assembled into full-length proteins against a related reference, which supplies the order of the pieces and fills the gaps the reads cannot cover.

title: Transformer (AR)
text: Autoregressive transformer decoders, which emit the peptide one residue at a time conditioned on the spectrum and on the residues already chosen. The dominant architecture since Casanovo, and the one

title: Transformer (encoder-only)
text: Transformer spectrum encoders trained without a decoder, usually self-supervised, to produce representations of a spectrum that other tasks reuse. The output is an embedding, not a peptide.

title: Transformer (NAR)

title: Antibodyomics
text: Antibody and antibody-repertoire sequencing, where the variable regions are by definition absent from any reference proteome. 50 catalogued workflows and 62 papers.

title: Astrobiology / life detection
text: Peptide biosignatures, where nothing about the target sequence can be assumed in advance. 2 catalogued workflows and 2 papers.

title: Bioactive peptides
text: Peptides with a function worth finding, from food hydrolysates to amphibian skin secretions. 81 catalogued workflows and 84 papers.

title: Food authentication
text: Telling species and processing apart in food, using peptide markers that survive cooking. 8 catalogued workflows and 9 papers.

title: Forensics
text: Attributing a trace to its source, from body fluids to the microbial signature of a place. 4 catalogued workflows and 5 papers.

title: General proteomics
text: Ordinary discovery proteomics, where de novo sequencing fills in what the database search could not explain. 80 catalogued workflows and 81 papers.

title: Glycoproteomics
text: Glycopeptides, where the glycan has to be accounted for before the peptide backbone can be read. 2 catalogued workflows and 2 papers.

title: Immunopeptidomics / neoantigen
text: HLA-presented peptides, where non-specific processing makes the search space too large for a database and the interesting peptides are the ones not in it. 26 catalogued workflows and 31 papers.

title: Metaproteomics
text: Mixed microbial communities, where which organisms are present is part of the question. 12 catalogued workflows and 16 papers.

title: Neuropeptidomics
text: Neuropeptides and hormones, which are short, modified and easy to miss in a database search. 10 catalogued workflows and 10 papers.

title: Palaeoproteomics
text: Ancient enamel, bone and eggshell, where the proteins are damaged and the species may be extinct. 14 catalogued workflows and 14 papers.

title: Clinical pathogen ID
text: Identifying the organism behind an infection directly from the sample. 3 catalogued workflows and 3 papers.

title: Plant-pathogen effectors
text: Effector proteins secreted by plant pathogens, often from organisms with no usable reference. 4 catalogued workflows and 5 papers.

title: Toxin identification (biodefense)
text: Recognising protein toxins in an unknown sample, where a database search presumes what you are looking for. 1 catalogued workflow and 1 paper.

title: Venomics
text: Venom from snakes, spiders, scorpions, ants and cone snails, where the species has no sequenced genome and the toxins are heavily modified. 50 catalogued workflows and 50 papers.

title: Wastewater metaproteomics
text: Wastewater as a population-level sample, carrying both microbial and human peptides. 1 catalogued workflow and 1 paper.

title: Wildlife proteomics
text: Milk, pouch and secretion proteomes of non-model animals, where reference proteomes are sparse or absent. 7 catalogued workflows and 7 papers.
